sessionGroups.name: May 11–18
sessionGroups.phase: Baseline city
sessionGroups.note: 27 short urban drives establishing the cell-spread reference baseline.

sessionGroups.name: May 23–31
sessionGroups.phase: First highway runs
sessionGroups.note: First sustained highway driving; traction-motor-temperature logging begins May 31.

sessionGroups.name: Jun 3
sessionGroups.phase: Cool-day city
sessionGroups.note: Coldest June city drives.

sessionGroups.name: Jun 9–14
sessionGroups.phase: Highway-intensive week
sessionGroups.note: Six days of heavy highway use — the bulk of cycle accumulation; peak engine-load and boost records set here. [M62 (2026-07-28): drive count corrected 17→18; the km total was already right for all 18 drives, so only the count had drifted.]

sessionGroups.name: Jun 16–18
sessionGroups.phase: Return to city
sessionGroups.note: Short city errands, all within a few days of the preceding highway sessions. Relevant to the SoC-band persistence question: these drives sit 50–97 h downstream of the last highway drive, well outside the window in which the highway ceiling elevation is still detectable (M59). See “What This Dataset Established” item 7.

sessionGroups.name: Jun 19
sessionGroups.phase: Long road trip
sessionGroups.note: 696 km single-day highway trip; best efficiency (2.76), 284 km longest single drive, 198 A dual-channel transient (33.9C v3).

sessionGroups.name: Jun 20–25
sessionGroups.phase: Extended daily city driving
sessionGroups.note: 207 km highway return plus city errands. Jun 22: cabin-soak thermal. Jun 24: cool overnight-park confirmed. Jun 25 D4: 139 km/h burst followed by 19s regen deceleration (93.2C peak, engine OFF) — 48% of charge energy from regen, highest in dataset; engine coolant 95°C.

sessionGroups.name: Jun 27
sessionGroups.phase: Major highway day
sessionGroups.note: Three long highway legs (184+127+121km) bracketed by city errands. Most drives in a single day (7). New records: max speed 146km/h, boost 1.51 bar, Sensor-1 49°C, dual-channel 199 A (34C v3) at 143km/h. Jun 19 remains the longest-distance (695.5km) and highest-cycle (26.7) single day.

sessionGroups.name: Jun 29 – Jul 07
sessionGroups.phase: Return to city errands
sessionGroups.note: Short urban/mixed errands after the Jun27 highway day (Jun29 3×, Jul02 2×, Jul05 2×, Jul07 2×). Jul07 D1: 17.2km mixed, 131km/h burst, 6.1s above 130, 43.9% regen share; D2 short urban with thermal carryover. All ens-clean.

sessionGroups.name: Jul 09 – Jul 11
sessionGroups.phase: Mixed + highway re-engagement
sessionGroups.note: Jul09 D1: 32.7km mixed, widest SoC excursion of the study to date (44.5→80.0→57.5%, soc_band 35.5pp). Jul11 (3 drives, 197.3km): two mixed_highway legs at 137–138km/h plus a mixed drive; deficit ~51% on both highway legs. All ens_outlier_v2-clean.

sessionGroups.name: Jul 12 – Jul 13
sessionGroups.phase: City-dominant close of window
sessionGroups.note: Jul12 (4 drives, 53.6km urban) and Jul13 (4 drives, 86.4km, same-day D1→D4 chain). Jul13 D4 set a new dataset-maximum 80–120km/h deficit (67.7%, M14-valid, 188.8s band), surpassing the prior 63.6% (May31 D2). All ens_outlier_v2-clean. Closes the observation window at Jul 13 (audit H-04: sessionGroups previously ended at Jun 27).

sessionGroups.name: Jul 14
sessionGroups.phase: City errands + high-speed highway record
sessionGroups.note: Jul14 D1–D3: three short urban legs (2.7/1.8/5.7km, amb 24°C, SoC bands 10.0–28.0pp). D4 (9.7km mixed_highway, amb 25°C): dataset-maximum speed 170.0km/h (prior max 146.0km/h), 103s total time ≥130km/h (raw 1Hz), 56.1s of that as battery-discharge time (engine-on) per highspeed_discharge_s_130p; 80–120km/h band time (67.2s) below the M14 120s gate, so its 53.1% deficit is excluded from the deficit aggregate. Net draw on D4 still net-regen (-1.86 kWh/100km corr2p) despite the excursion. All four ens_outlier_v2-clean. Closes the observation window at Jul 14 (supersedes the Jul 12–13 close). —— M62 (2026-07-28, ledger reconciliation): this narrative describes D1–D4 only. Five further Jul-14 drives were ingested afterwards without this row being updated, so the count/km above previously read 4 / 19.9 km against a master holding 9 / 65.9 km. The undocumented remainder (D5–D9, 14:59–17:02) is 5 urban legs totalling 46.0 km / 1.19 h / GTC 4.9944: 3.9, 17.6, 15.7, 5.5 and 3.3 km, speed max 93 km/h, SoC bands 11.0–29.0 pp, engine-on 26.4–58.3%, pack-mean peak climbing 34.8→41.5°C across the afternoon. All five are ens_outlier_v2-clean. The earlier claim that this session “closes the observation window at Jul 14” stands for the window, not for the drive count.

sessionGroups.name: Jul 15–16
sessionGroups.phase: Sustained-highway re-engagement
sessionGroups.note: Jul15 (2 drives, 83.2km) plus the Jul16 8-drive day (578.0km) — the second-largest single-day distance of the study after Jun19 (695.5km), and its largest by drive count tied with Jun27 (8 vs 7). Three long legs (D2 200.9km, D4 175.7km, D3 159.7km) bracketed by five short urban errands. Jul16 D2 set the dataset's longest continuous high-speed streaks — 97s ≥130km/h and 46s ≥140km/h, peaking at 147.0km/h — the first entry into the 140+ band under continuous rather than transient conditions (Jul14 D4's 170km/h remains the point maximum). This narrows but does not close the M-series 'sustained 140+ km/h' coverage gap: corpus-wide dwell ≥140km/h is still only 114s across 6 drives, far short of thermal steady state. Pack peaked at 42.2°C pack-mean / 47°C (Sensor 1) on D4 at 29–30°C ambient. All 10 drives ens_outlier_v2-clean. Closes the observation window at Jul 16 (supersedes the Jul 14 close).

sessionGroups.name: Jul 17
sessionGroups.phase: Congestion-duty urban
sessionGroups.note: Three short stop-and-go legs (5.2 / 3.7 / 1.5km) at 24→30°C ambient, a return to pure city duty after the Jul 15–16 highway block. Distinguished by unusually low moving means (15.5–17.4km/h) and high stationary fractions (27.7–40.4%) — D2 is the 5th-lowest moving mean of the 141-drive corpus. No highway-band time on any drive (80–120 band 0.0s throughout), so the batch adds nothing to the M14 deficit aggregate (deficitValidN unchanged at 43) and nothing to the 140+ km/h coverage gap. D2's 44.0% soc_min ties the dataset floor and reinforces the ~44% lower bound of the BMS operating window. Thermally benign: pack-mean peaks 28.2–30.2°C despite 30°C ambient, tracking intake rather than load. All three ens_outlier_v2-clean. Dash odometer 39,849km as of Jul 17 (+11km vs the Jul 16 reading of 39,838km; OBD trip distance sums to 10.4km over the same interval — within the 1km dash quantization). Closes the observation window at Jul 17 (supersedes the Jul 15–16 close).

sessionGroups.name: Jul 18
sessionGroups.phase: Mixed urban + highway day-cycle
sessionGroups.note: Eight drives spanning a full day (11:32→22:03) across a 17–31°C ambient sweep — the widest single-day thermal span in the corpus. Two mid-day mixed-highway legs (D3 60.8km, D5 50.4km; max 126/119km/h) bracket six short urban trips, restoring highway-band sampling after the Jul 17 pure-urban batch. D3 and D5 each clear the M14 ≥120s gate (1085s and 499.6s of 80–120 band), lifting deficitValidN from 43 to 45; their band deficits (46.7%, 59.6%) sit inside the corpus range and neither drive approaches the 140+ km/h regime (both cap at ≤126km/h), so the high-speed thermal steady-state gap remains untouched. Urban legs show the expected creep/idle signature — throughput-per-100km of 42–43 on the shortest trips driven by 23–36% stationary fractions, not an efficiency change (M35); the highway legs sit at 14.9–17.5/100km. D8 (1.8km, 356.9s) is the batch's only ens_outlier_v2 (ens_extreme), flagged by the intensity taxonomy on a per-km artifact (net corr2p +8.62kWh/100km) rather than the hard domain rules; the other seven are v2-clean. soc_min bottoms at 44.5% (D6), 0.5pp above the 44.0% dataset floor — consistent with the ~44% BMS lower bound. vreg_R_pack on the five load-excited drives spans 96.41–126.30mΩ, consistent with the ~124mΩ corpus level; no single-drive resistance requires T-/I-controlled OLS-residual adjudication this batch (unlike Jul17 D1). Thermally the evening highway leg D5 records the batch's hottest traction motor (92°C) and pack-mean peak (45.5°C) despite a falling 30→26°C ambient, tracking sustained load rather than road speed alone. Two-pass current-sensor offset recalibrates to −0.3968A (from −0.4017 at n=141; sign and order preserved). Dash odometer 39,999km as of Jul 18 (+150 vs Jul 17's 39,849; OBD trip distance sums to 148.0km over the interval — within the 1km dash quantization). Extends the observation window to Jul 18 (supersedes the Jul 17 close).

sessionGroups.name: Jul 19
sessionGroups.phase: Evening urban duty-cycle
sessionGroups.note: Six urban legs (15:44→21:41) across a 19–24°C ambient, all pure-city duty following the Jul 18 mixed-highway day. No drive holds the 80–120 highway band for ≥120s (D3 peaks at 11.4s of band time), so the M14 aggregate is unchanged (deficitValidN stays 45) and the 140+ km/h steady-state gap is untouched — batch speed_max caps at 84km/h. D4 (20:50, 20.1km) sets a NEW corpus SoC floor of 43.5%, 0.5pp below the prior 44.0% floor (previously tied by May17 D1 / Jul14 D1 / Jul17 D2), marginally extending the observed BMS lower operating bound from ~44% to ~43.5%. Thermally moderate but rising: pack-mean peaks climb 31.2→39.0°C across the batch as the later legs run on a heat-soaked pack; D4 records the batch's hottest traction motor (88°C) on its 20.1km continuous run despite a 20°C ambient, tracking accumulated load rather than road speed. Three drives excite the vreg estimator (D1 145.53, D3 125.84, D4 129.56mΩ, all inside the ~126mΩ corpus level); the three sub-1.5km legs carry no load samples. All six ens_outlier_v2-clean. Two-pass current-sensor offset recalibrates to −0.3926A (from −0.3968 at n=149; sign and order preserved). Dash odometer 40,059km as of Jul 19 (+60 vs Jul 18's 39,999; OBD trip distance sums to 59.5km — within the 1km dash quantization). Extends the observation window to Jul 19 (supersedes the Jul 18 close).

sessionGroups.name: Jul 20
sessionGroups.phase: Urban day-cycle with two highway/rural legs
sessionGroups.note: Six drives (11:38→21:53) across a 13–24°C ambient — the day's steepest single-day drop, from a 24°C midday peak to 13°C by the final evening leg. D2 (159.5km, 3.5% highway/36.6% urban time-weighted) is the largest single drive added since the corpus-record 284.2km Jun19 leg, and alone contributes GTC 13.3524 to the day's total; D3 (43.3km) is the day's second highway/rural leg. D2 and D3 both clear the 80–120 band ≥120s validity floor (1597.3s and 375.2s respectively), pushing deficitValidN from 45 to 47 — the first new deficit-valid drives since the corpus baseline. D3 sets a NEW corpus thermal ceiling: pack-mean 45.8°C and T1 51.0°C, surpassing the prior 45.5°C / 50.0°C record (Jul18 single mixed-highway leg) by 0.3°C / 1.0°C — consistent with sustained high-speed running (max 123km/h) rather than ambient (24→22°C, unremarkable). D6, the day's coolest-ambient leg (17→13°C), posts the lowest vreg_R_pack of the batch (96.56mΩ) alongside the day's hottest traction motor (90°C) after a 64min continuous run — heat accumulation, not ambient, driving the motor peak. All six drives ens_outlier_v2-clean. Two-pass current-sensor offset recalibrates to −0.4006A (from −0.3926A at n=155; sign and order preserved).

sessionGroups.name: Jul 21
sessionGroups.phase: Mild urban duty-cycle
sessionGroups.note: Six urban legs (11:43→20:26), 36.8km, on a mild and narrow 20–22°C ambient — no highway/rural running, in contrast to Jul20's two long mixed legs. D2 (0.9km, 443.8s) trips the standard domain rule (distance_km<1.0 & duration_s>300) and is flagged ens_outlier_v2/ens_invalid — the batch's only flag; the other five, including a comparably short 1.0km/249.3s D4, stay under the duration threshold and remain clean. D6 ties (does not break) the corpus SoC floor of 43.5%, first set by Jul19 D4. No drive holds the 80–120 band ≥120s, so deficitValidN is unchanged at 47 (all growth this batch came from Jul20's D2/D3). Thermally quiet relative to Jul20: pack-mean tops out at 35.0°C (D6) and T1 at 36.0°C, both well inside the new 45.8°C/51.0°C ceiling set the day before. D1's cool 26°C pack (morning start) posts the day's highest vreg_R_pack (158.20mΩ), consistent with the corpus's inverse T–R fit. Two-pass current-sensor offset recalibrates to −0.3994A (from −0.4006A at n=161; sign and order preserved). Dash odometer 40,384km as of Jul 21 (+325 vs Jul 19's 40,059; combined Jul20+Jul21 OBD trip distance sums to 321.2km — a 3.8km gap, larger than the ~1km single-day dash quantization typically seen but proportionate for a 325km/2-day span and within the expected dash-vs-OBD tracking tolerance). Extends the observation window to Jul 21 (supersedes the Jul 19 close); corpus now 167 drives / 4,644.7km / 712.02kWh gross throughput / GTC 339.06.

sessionGroups.name: Jul 22
sessionGroups.phase: Cool urban duty-cycle
sessionGroups.note: Six urban legs (12:13→21:15), 16.3km, on a cool 14–18°C ambient falling monotonically through the day — the lowest ambient band of any late-July session and, at a 26.0°C pack-mean peak, the coolest multi-drive session in the corpus (prior sub-27°C days — Jun 3/16/17/18 — were all 2-drive sessions). Thermally this sits 19.8°C below the 45.8°C pack ceiling set on Jul 20, and T1 (27.0°C) sits 24.0°C below the 51.0°C sensor ceiling; neither is challenged. No highway running at all (pct_highway 0.0 on all six), continuing the urban-only pattern established Jul 21. D5 (0.7km, 199.8s) is the batch's only flag — ens_outlier_v2 / ens_extreme, but ens_invalid False: it trips no hard domain rule (duration 199.8s is under the 300s threshold that caught Jul 21's D2) and is flagged by the statistical arm of the M23 ensemble instead. Its distinguishing feature is engine_on_pct 0.0% — the generator never started, making it the corpus's fourth engine-off drive and the first moving one since 20260514_093059 (1.3km). The resulting +15.37/100km net corr2p is the arithmetic consequence of an unreplenished buffer on a sub-1km denominator, and reinforces the M35 rationale for treating gross throughput — not net draw — as the canonical efficiency metric. No drive holds the 80–120km/h band for ≥120s (D4's 2.3s is the batch total), so deficitValidN is unchanged at 47 for the third consecutive batch. Only D2 yields vreg samples (164.43mΩ, n=311) — the 4th-highest single-drive pack resistance recorded, consistent with the session's cold packs under the corpus inverse T–R fit and not indicative of fade; the temperature-controlled power-fade slope remains statistically indistinct (+1.61mΩ/month, CI [−0.86, +4.50], P(slope>0)=0.90, n=88). Degradation trending is likewise unmoved: adjusted loaded-spread slope +0.107mV/month, bootstrap CI [−0.81, +0.80], P(slope>0)=0.59 at n_clean=155 — still no statistically detectable divergence. Two-pass current-sensor offset recalibrates to −0.3987A (from −0.3994A at n=167; sign and order preserved, 3 drives excluded by domain rule). Dash odometer 40,401km as of Jul 22 (+17 vs Jul 21's 40,384) against 16.3km of OBD trip distance — a 0.7km gap, within single-day dash quantization. Extends the observation window to Jul 22; corpus now 173 drives / 4,661.0km / 716.74kWh gross throughput / GTC 341.31.

sessionGroups.name: Jul 23
sessionGroups.phase: Cool-evening long-leg mix, first split terrain signature
sessionGroups.note: Seven legs, 156.4km, spanning a 20C->10C ambient collapse across a single day - the widest one-day ambient range in the corpus, and a 10C-cooler floor than any prior late-July session. Volume rebounds an order of magnitude from Jul 22's 16.3km, making this the largest day since Jul 20. Structurally the batch splits in two. Three long legs (D1 56.7km, D3 34.1km, D7 43.1km, together 85% of the distance) run at 43-53km/h moving means with low stationary fractions; D3 and D7 draw 53.2% and 50.8% of pack charge from regeneration - the 96th and 94th percentiles of clean corpus drives >3km - while D3 simultaneously posts the batch's lowest engine-on fraction at 17.9%. Four short legs (D2, D4, D5, D6) show the opposite: regen 17.6-29.9% of charge, engine-on up to 52.6%. TERRAIN ATTRIBUTION (M52): the user reports hilly driving, and the drivetrain signature on the long legs is consistent with sustained descent (high regen share with the generator idle). It is NOT independently confirmed. The barometric channel cannot do so at any useful resolution - see forwardNotes.m52BaroAudit - and the batch-median terrain proxies are unremarkable against the corpus (regen share 51st percentile, SoC band per km 41st percentile), because the four short legs pull the median back. The signature is real per-drive on D3/D7 and absent on D5/D6; it should be reported that way rather than as a session property. Thermally unremarkable: 41.0C pack-mean / 45.0C T1 peak (D7) sit 4.8C and 6.0C below the Jul 20 corpus ceilings despite D7 running on the day's coldest ambient. SoC ceiling 83.0% (D2), 5.0pp below the 88.0% corpus record; D1 (79.5), D7 (82.0) and D2 (83.0) all sit at or above the M48 ~78-80% dissipation knee. No highway running (pct_highway 0.0 on all seven, speed_max 84km/h). D4 (0.4km, 108.5s) is the batch's only flag - ens_extreme, ens_invalid False. Dash odometer 40,559km as of Jul 23 (+158 vs Jul 22 40,401) against 156.4km of OBD trip distance — a 1.6km gap, within the expected dash-vs-OBD tracking tolerance for a 7-drive day. Extends the observation window to Jul 23; corpus now 180 drives / 4,817.4km / 752.84kWh gross throughput / GTC 358.49.

sessionGroups.name: Jul 24
sessionGroups.phase: Warm-to-cool scale split; regen-dominant long legs
sessionGroups.note: Five urban legs, 92.5km, over a single-day ambient descent from 16C midday to 10-12C by the last evening leg - a warmer floor than Jul 23's 10C collapse but the same cool-evening character. Volume falls back from Jul 23's 156.4km to a mid-sized day. The batch is structurally bimodal: two sub-2km micro-legs (D1, D2) that are essentially generator-management hops - D2 in particular is a pure net top-up (charge fraction 61.2%, net corrected draw -8.38 kWh/100km) - and three 27-33km legs (D3, D4, D5) that carry 97% of the distance at 40-45km/h moving means. The defining signature of the substantive legs is regeneration dominance: D4 and D5 draw 50.4% and 51.2% of pack charge from regen, D3 35.9%, placing D4/D5 near the top decile of clean corpus drives >3km, while their engine-on fractions (35.1%, 32.9%) sit at the batch floor. This is the inverse of the short-leg pattern (D1 regen 2.8%, D2 12.3%) and consistent with longer coast/decel opportunity on the extended routes. All three long legs clip the SoC ceiling-defence band (max 79.0/81.0/81.5%, M46 knee) despite none exceeding 86km/h. Thermally the day is unremarkable: pack-mean peaks track leg length (18.8/22.0C micro; 36.8/39.8/38.0C long) and the evening D5 still reaches 38.0C pack from its own dissipation despite the coolest ambient of the day, reaffirming that pack warming here is drive-driven rather than ambient-driven. Motor peak 86.0C (D3) is the batch high. All five are ens_outlier_v2-clean; none carry a valid 80-120 deficit (zero highway exposure). Corpus after ingestion: 185 drives, 4909.9km, 775.11 kWh gross throughput, GTC 369.10, 2026-05-11 -> 2026-07-24. The M24 two-pass current-sensor offset recalibrated to -0.4008 A (from -0.414 A pre-Jul-23), within the expected drift band for corpus expansion; ens_outlier_v2 count 8/185.

sessionGroups.name: Jul 25
sessionGroups.phase: Single dominant highway leg + urban support; first sustained 80-120 band exposure of late July
sessionGroups.note: Five legs, 222.9km, over a warm midday-to-late-afternoon window (16-24C, no cold content). Volume rebounds from Jul 24's 92.5km, driven almost entirely by one dominant highway-weighted leg. The day is structurally the inverse of the Jul 23/24 pattern: instead of a bimodal split of short hops plus several mid-length urban legs, it is one 152.3km mixed_highway leg (D4, 68% of distance, highway_like) plus four urban support legs (2-50km). D4 is the batch's sole carrier of highway-band exposure and thermal maxima: 2647s (44.1min) in the 80-120km/h band (deficit_80_120 46.3%) - the first substantial highway-band contribution since the late-July run began - pack-mean 41.2C / T1 46.0C peak and engine coolant 98C / oil 102C, all batch maxima, and the largest single-drive rf_efc (5.6525). Its 14.94 kWh/100km throughput is the batch's most efficient, consistent with sustained cruise. Critically its speed_max is 113km/h with highspeed_discharge_s_130p=0.0: the sustained 140+km/h regime and any >130km/h sampling remain uncaptured, so this leg does not close the corpus's high-speed gap. The four urban legs span the expected short-trip behaviour: D2/D3 net-charging or generator-dominated top-ups, D1 the widest SoC band of the batch (36.0pp) with soc_max 81.0 clipping the M46 knee, and D5 a 2.0km micro-leg flagged ens_extreme (ens_invalid False - statistical arm only, the standard sub-2km denominator artefact). Thermally the urban legs are unremarkable (pack-mean 36.0-39.2C); the day's thermal ceiling is set by D4's duration and load, not ambient. No winter or sub-15C content - the corpus's #1 gap (cold-start) is untouched by this batch, and the #2 gap (sustained 140+km/h) is approached but not met. Corpus after ingestion: 190 drives, 5132.8km, 814.83 kWh gross throughput, GTC 388.0, 2026-05-11 -> 2026-07-25. Dash odometer 40,905km. The M24 two-pass current-sensor offset recalibrated to -0.4029 A (from -0.4008 A at Jul 24, n=185), within the expected drift band for a +5-drive expansion; ens_outlier_v2 count 9/190 (D5 the sole new flag).

sessionGroups.name: Jul 26
sessionGroups.phase: First sustained 140+ km/h sampling; buffer throughput decoupled from distance
sessionGroups.note: Four legs, 690.7km / 9.01h, 79.56 kWh gross, GTC 37.89 - the corpus's second-largest day by distance (behind Jun 19's 695.5km) and the first to sample a sustained high-speed regime. Warm throughout: ambient 19 -> 28C by midday, easing to 20C on the evening leg; intake 25.8 -> 30.4C. Structurally the day is two long carriers plus two mid-length legs, all four k3 highway_like and all four ens_outlier_v2-clean. D1 (220.0km) and D2 (222.0km) are the corpus's #3 and #2 longest single drives and together carry 64% of the day's distance. The day's analytic value is twofold. First, high-speed coverage: D2 and D3 both reached 157 km/h, D2 held 130+ km/h for 142.6s (2.5x the previous per-drive corpus maximum) with a 53s unbroken >=140 km/h hold, doubling corpus >=140 occupancy from 114s to 229s. Second, an unusually clean natural experiment on buffer duty: D1 and D2 cover near-identical distance but D1 pushes 14.19 kWh/100km through the pack against D2's 7.82 - a 1.8x spread driven entirely by engine duty cycle (56.2% vs 78.6% engine-on; 126 vs 61 engine-off runs). Throughput tracks how often the generator is available to feed the motor directly, not how far the vehicle travelled. Thermals stayed moderate for the load: pack-mean peaks 38.8-42.5C against the 45.8C corpus record, motor peak 94C on D2.

sessionGroups.name: Aug 1
sessionGroups.phase: Single evening leg reopening the corpus after a 6-day gap
sessionGroups.note: One leg, 24.1km / 0.49h, 4.01 kWh gross, GTC 1.9104 - reopens the corpus after a 6-day gap (last drive Jul 26; the intervening Jul 30 B/D-mode comparison run is excluded by convention). Warm evening commute, ambient constant 31C, mixed_highway / k3 highway_like, ens_outlier_v2-clean. Speed_max 135km/h is the drive's ceiling but 130+ content is negligible (highspeed_discharge_s_130p 1.8s) - no material change to the corpus's sparse >=140km/h census left at 229s after Jul 26. 28.6% highway / 51.5% urban by time, 21.6% stationary - a traffic-heavy evening leg despite the nominal highway content. SoC band 25.0pp (49.0-74.0). Pack-mean peak only 32.0C, mild for the top-speed reading, reflecting the short 29.1-minute duration. Engine-on 43.4%, regen 46.8% of charge. Throughput 16.65 kWh/100km.

sessionGroups.name: Aug 2
sessionGroups.phase: Corpus-record diurnal ambient swing; sustained highway leg isolates buffer duty from short-trip inflation; pack thermal lag demonstrated within a single day
sessionGroups.note: Eight legs, 228.9km / 4.07h, 37.56 kWh gross, GTC 17.888. The day's defining feature is its ambient arc: 18C on both morning legs, climbing to a 34-35C midday/afternoon peak, holding 32C into early evening, then easing 32->29->27C through the close - an 18C range that is the widest single-day ambient swing yet logged in the corpus, surpassing Jul 18's 14C. All eight legs are ens_outlier_v2-clean. Structurally, one leg carries the day: D3 (158.1km, 69.1% of distance, k3 highway_like, 65.6% engine-on) is the day's sole 80-120km/h-band contributor (3743.1s, deficit 49.3%) and posts the day's best per-100km throughput (13.81) against 18.4-33.6 kWh/100km on the seven short urban/mixed legs - most of that spread a short-trip denominator artefact (M35) rather than a real efficiency signal. The more durable finding is thermal: pack-mean climbs from 25.2C at the 08:12 start to a 42.8C ceiling at 19:37 (D7, on the cooling 29C evening leg, not the 34-35C midday peak) and is still 41.0C by the 21:34 close (27C ambient) - well under the corpus's 45.8C record, but a clean within-day demonstration that pack temperature tracks cumulative load and lags ambient by hours, not one drive's instantaneous conditions. Two short morning urban commutes (D1, D2, 7.0km) were appended to the corpus under M80 prior to this session; the six afternoon/evening legs (D3-D8, 221.9km) are new.

sessionGroups.name: Aug 3
sessionGroups.phase: Homogeneous warm-evening urban/mixed batch; pack thermal-lag reproduced at single-day scale as ambient falls
sessionGroups.note: Three evening legs, 80.2km / 1.94h, 16.45 kWh gross, GTC 7.8346. A deliberately homogeneous batch - all three urban/mixed legs of 25-28km, k3 mixed_like, ens_outlier_v2-clean - with no morning or midday coverage, so ambient stays in a narrow 24-31C warm-evening band (D1 29->31->29, D2 29, D3 27->24) rather than Aug 2's 18C diurnal arc. Re-assessed on a gross-capacity-turnover basis (GTC = total charge+discharge throughput / one nominal pack energy, 2.1 kWh — counts regen charge as cell stress). NOTE (audit 2026-07-14): GTC is NOT the conventional full-equivalent-cycle count (FCE = throughput / 2×nominal), and the 20,000-"cycle" reference is an unverified generic-lithium planning threshold whose own cycle convention and test conditions are not established for this pack — the model-specific Nissan sources identify the battery only as Li-ion, not NMC. The dashboard’s SELECTED blend scenario (renamed from “realistic blend”, M56 — it is a hand-chosen forward-usage assumption, not the observed duty cycle) reaches that threshold at the rate and age computed live in summary_arrays.cycleLife, but this is a labeled assumption scenario, NOT a rated end-of-life. Treat it as a directional floor only: it does not yet reflect winter cold-start driving (sub-zero starts, high C-rate on a cold pack, short trips) — the dataset’s #1 named risk — and the depth-weighted rainflow view (M17) suggests the flat gross-turnover convention is conservative for this shallow-buffering duty cycle. Even as a floor, ~9–10 yr is a substantial service life. A defensible SOH figure requires the controlled capacity/HPPC reference campaign, not this counter. M56 (2026-07-26, audit F-05/P0-2): the hardcoded ~2,090 GTC/yr and ~9.6yr figures were stale duplicates of pipeline outputs and have been removed from this hand-maintained note; the live values are bound from summary_arrays.cycleLife in the dashboard. M56 (audit F-04) additionally carries the OBSERVED logged distance mix as an explicit scenario, which crosses the same unverified threshold materially later than the selected blend — the gap between the two is a scenario-choice effect, not new evidence about the pack. M62 (2026-07-28, terminology audit): GTC is NOT a recognised battery metric — a literature search returns only “gross capacity” in the unrelated nameplate-vs-usable sense. The industry standard is the equivalent full cycle (EFC), which is discharge-referenced and counts depth (one 100% DoD cycle, two 50% cycles and ten 10% cycles all equal 1 EFC). On this corpus the study's FCE is the metric that maps onto that standard (FCE/EFC_standard = 1.029, the residual being charge/discharge asymmetry), whereas GTC = 2.058 × standard EFC by construction. The 20,000 figure is therefore a threshold in a non-standard unit AND without provenance; expressed in standard EFC it is ~10,000. Live values bind from summary_arrays.metricConvention.

M40 (2026-07-16, n=138). Resting spread median ~10.6 mV across the 133 drives carrying the cell-voltage channel. Loaded p95 ceiling 34.0 mV. The M19 clustered-bootstrap trend on the adjusted loaded spread remains statistically indistinguishable from zero — Huber basis −0.309 mV/month, 95% CI [−1.329, +0.388], P(slope>0)=0.21, n_clean=119; OLS basis −0.348 mV/month, 95% CI [−1.408, +0.361], P(slope>0)=0.18, n_clean=122 (report the CI, not a point estimate) — read this as "no resolved trend in the short observation window," not "no degradation."

seasonalAssumptions._provenance: M28 (2026-07-10). Inputs for the all-year seasonal cycle-life extrapolation. monthlyTempC = user-supplied Kyiv monthly mean daily temperatures (external climatology; NOT measured by this study; note it diverges by up to 1.1C from the older archived 'climate' block, which is retained unchanged per provenance convention). All model parameters below are assumptions carried with lo/mid/hi bands because the cold tail below the lowest logged pack-probe reading is modelled, not observed; consumptionSlopePerC is anchored to the 15-30% hybrid winter consumption penalty range reported in cold-climate fleet literature, coldSoakRetention encodes inter-drive pack cooling under the 5-6 short-city-drives/day working pattern, and platingDamageWeights are generic NMC low-temperature stress multipliers (sensitivity only, not fitted to this pack).

hotTail._provenance: M85 (2026-08-05): high-temperature cycle-damage sensitivity, symmetric to the cold platingDamageWeights. Unlike the cold tail, this one is MEASURED: the logged corpus is almost entirely Warm and Shoulder ambient class (Cold-class drives are below minimum support), so pack thermal exposure is characterised directly for that range (time-weighted mean pack ~34.2C, 54.3% of drive-time >=35C, highway thermal rise +17C above ambient). A hot class-month is one whose modeled pack temp (ambient + measured per-class rise) exceeds tempThresholdC; its cycles are damage-weighted either by the per-temp Arrhenius factor (arrhenius block, Ea/refC) or by the flatDamageWeights ladder. Reported as a labelled sensitivity only, never folded into the primary crossing (same discipline as plating). This is a CYCLE-damage overlay; the calendar-aging axis (calendarLifeYrShaded) is duty-blended and dominated by the parked/winter state, so it is NOT changed by this term.
hotTail.note: High-T stress is the in-drive cycling accelerant (pack does its charge/discharge work at ~35C, ~1.95x calendar-basis Arrhenius acceleration vs 25C). It is distinct from and opposite to the cold plating tail; both are carried so the two ends of the temperature axis are visible.

It does NOT re-execute and does NOT prove reproducibility for: (1) the statsmodels-based degradation trends (degradation_trends.py -- cluster-robust OLS, mixed-effects GLM, TOST equivalence), which depend on the pinned statsmodels version recorded in packageVersions above (a statsmodels/scipy upgrade can shift numerical optimizer paths for the mixed-effects fit even with a fixed random seed); (2) energy_uncertainty_mc.py / energy_mc_precompute.py Monte Carlo draws, which are seeded but not covered by this harness; (3) m119v2_model.py (M119-v2 socHysteresisV2), which is frozen/carried-forward and not refit by default (see socHysteresisV2.recomputePolicy), including its own M222.1 rolling-origin CV re-fits and M222.2 detector reconciliation; (4) interDriveCarryover's (M223.1) day-clustered bootstrap OLS (seeded, seed=42) and its secondary day random-intercept mixed-effects check, which shares the same statsmodels-version sensitivity as (1) and separately can fail to converge on a singular random-effects covariance at low pairs-per-day density (observed and reported as such, not a reproducibility failure of this harness); (5) regimeTransition's (M223.2) day-block-preserving permutation test (seeded, seed=42, 4000 draws) and its Dirichlet/day-clustered-bootstrap per-cell uncertainty intervals (seeded, 1000 draws), neither re-executed here; (6) dailyFingerprints' (M227.2) k-means clustering (seed=42) and its day-bootstrap adjusted-Rand-index stability check (200 resamples, seed=42), neither re-executed here. Treat this block as scoped evidence for the ML16 exclusion set only, not a whole-pipeline determinism proof.
determinism.note: Generated live by determinism_check.py on the current 489-drive master. postprocess_master() is run twice from scratch; the ML16 ensemble (KMeans k=3 n_init=20, IsolationForest 500 trees contamination 0.06, LOF n_neighbors=15, MAD gates) is seeded (random_state=42), so the two runs are bit-identical and the canonical exclusion reproduces exactly by file identity. Validity is conditional on packageVersions. See reproducibilityScope for what this proof does and does not cover.

officialDisclosure._provenance: M79 (2026-07-31). External regulatory disclosure, NOT measured by this study. Nissan X-Trail e-POWER (T33) battery performance and durability table, filed under Article 10, Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 (the EU Batteries Regulation). Transcribed from the manufacturer's published compliance table (image source reviewed 2026-07-31; no public URL captured this session). Figures are the manufacturer's own test-protocol outputs; the source table states no warranty implication can be derived from any value in it, and this study repeats that disclaimer rather than treating any figure as a guarantee.
officialDisclosure.note: Capacity fade / power fade / internal-resistance increase are all defined AT the 14yr / 190,000km condition, not as a linear rate; this study's officialDisclosureCorrelation.resistance.trendContext uses a linear-in-throughput approximation only to sanity-check whether the measured M25 null result is consistent with the disclosed life-point figure at the CURRENT mileage, not to restate the disclosure as a rate.

batterySupplier._provenance: M79 (2026-07-31). Vehicle Energy Japan (VE-J) news release, 2023-09-19 -- 2023 Nissan Global Supplier Award, Global Innovation Award, for battery cells/modules supplying the Nissan X-Trail e-POWER system.
batterySupplier.awardName: 2023 Nissan Global Supplier Award -- Global Innovation Award
batterySupplier.productDescription: Lithium-ion battery cells and modules; the award citation names high output, safety, and long life as the optimal technology solution for the X-Trail e-POWER system, i.e. a power-optimised cell design, not an energy-optimised one.
batterySupplier.note: Neither Nissan nor VE-J material reviewed publishes cathode chemistry/stoichiometry. VE-J is the former Hitachi Automotive Systems battery business, historically a high-power laminate cell line for HEV/e-POWER applications -- consistent with a high-power layered-oxide (NMC/NCA-class) cell, but NOT a confirmation of cathode chemistry. This study's telemetry EXCLUDES LFP (3.50-4.11 V cell window) but cannot uniquely identify the cathode; OEM material discloses only lithium-ion.

socLevelWeighting._provenance: M91 (2026-08-06). Cross-check against Wikner (Chalmers, 2017, licentiate thesis: 'Lithium ion Battery Aging: Battery Lifetime Testing and Physics-based Modeling for Electric Vehicle Applications', https://publications.lib.chalmers.se/records/fulltext/249356/249356.pdf) -- NMC/LMO-blend graphite pouch cell, 26 Ah, automotive-grade, comparable chemistry family to this pack's VE-J-disclosed NMC fingerprint (M79) but a different cell/format. Her 10%-SOC-interval lifetime cycling data show SoC WINDOW LEVEL is a comparably strong -- at points dominant -- aging axis, independent of DOD: intervals below ~30% SoC show minimal cycling aging (several cells did not reach EOL within the project's cycling budget), while intervals at/above ~50% show clearly accelerated aging with little further separation above ~60%. The rf_damage_k2 Woehler-DoD proxy (M17) is blind to this axis: it weights a cycle purely by depth, so an equal-depth cycle at 15-20% SoC and at 60-65% SoC score identically. M91 adds the diagnostic split (drive_master.csv columns rf_damage_k2_socband_{lo,mid,hi}, rf_socmean_wtd_pct) and this weight-sensitivity block. NEITHER changes rf_damage_k2 itself or any primary crossing -- both are labeled, unverified sensitivities, same discipline as platingDamageWeights / hotTail.flatDamageWeights. Wikner's %-breakpoints and the weight multipliers below are approximate, qualitative, and not fitted to this pack; her tests were fixed 10%-window symmetric CC cycling, not this pack's continuously-varying shallow buffering, so treat as directional only, never as a calibrated correction.
socLevelWeighting.weightLadderNote: Three paired scenarios (index-matched across lo/mid/hi): [0] unweighted (=rf_damage_k2, sanity anchor), [1] mild -- Wikner's qualitative direction at low multiplier, [2] Wikner-consistent -- low-SoC cycling ~2x less damaging, high-SoC cycling ~2x more damaging than the unweighted depth-only estimate, per her data's rough order of magnitude. NOT a fitted correction; carried as a labeled sensitivity ladder only.

kExponentLadder.plausibilityCeilingBasis: calendarLifeYrShaded (seasonalLife, M28) — calendar aging alone ends the pack near here regardless of cycling
kExponentLadder._provenance: M93 (2026-08-07). Consumed by compute_summary_arrays._k_ladder_scenarios to build the Woehler/S-N k-exponent sensitivity ladder that replaces the retired M91 SoC-level weight-ladder chart. k is the Woehler DoD depth-exponent (RF_DAMAGE_EXP in compute_drive_summary_v6, fixed at 2 for M17): NMC-GENERIC, NOT fitted to this pack's cells, hence verified:false on the output block. kGrid is bounded to the physically admissible NMC range 1.0..2.5 (k=1 = linear throughput / flat GTC convention, k=2 = current generic value, k=2.5 = plausible ceiling) plus k=3.0 as a FLAGGED aggressive upper extreme. floorPct MUST equal compute_drive_summary_v6.RF_FLOOR_PCT (1.0) so the k=1 rung reproduces rf_efc exactly and m(1)=1.0. referenceThresholdGtc must match fadeModes.capacity.thresholdGtc (itself unverified, SCENARIO_THRESHOLD_GTC). Diagnostic sensitivity ONLY: the function never folds any rung into rf_damage_k2, cycleLife, or a fadeModes crossing; remove this block to hide the panel under an arrays-only regen.

oemTechReview._provenance: M105 (2026-08-09). User-supplied primary source, not web-retrieved: Nissan Technical Review No.89 (2023), Special Feature 1 ("Tough Gear" and "High Quality" for New X-TRAIL), articles 1 (Yamamoto, "Evolution of genuine SUVs: New X-TRAIL e-4ORCE"), 2 (Yoshida/Hasegawa/Takaoka, "VC-TURBO and e-POWER System"), 3 (Ogino/Tsuchiya/Mizuno/Sakai/Abe, "Engine Evolution of e-POWER"), 4 (Katakura/Suzuki, "Application of e-4ORCE to Full-Scale SUVs"), 5 (Li/Suganuma/Kuwata/Funatsu/Fukuoka/Mitani/Maeda/Terashima/Igarashi/Okada, "NV Technology to Achieve EV-Level Quietness"). Manufacturer engineering-team publication, external to and independent of this study's own telemetry; used here the same way officialDisclosure/batterySupplier (M79) and the Wikner thesis (M91) are used elsewhere -- as a cross-check anchor for corpus findings, never as a source of new corpus data. Every figure below is paraphrased from the source, not quoted, and each is scoped to what it actually supports: several are JDM (domestic-market) or e-4ORCE-only (AWD) figures that do not directly transfer to this study's EU-market FWD (T33) primary corpus, and are flagged as such.
oemTechReview.scope: The powertrain layer described in Articles 1-3 and 5 (engine, generator, front motor, HV bus, energy management, NV strategy) is shared between the FWD and e-4ORCE variants -- one engine, one generator, one front motor in both. Article 4's torque-distribution / pitching-control material is AWD-specific (dual-motor e-4ORCE only) and is out of scope for the primary FWD corpus; it is retained here only for eventual use against the segregated e-4ORCE cross-check rail.

topologyConfirmation.claim: Series-hybrid topology: 100% of electric power generated by the engine, 100% of driving force delivered by the motor; engine has no mechanical path to the wheels.
topologyConfirmation.source: Article 2, §2 ("Overview and lineup of the e-POWER system"), Fig. 1.
topologyConfirmation.note: Direct manufacturer confirmation of this study's foundational architecture assumption -- the premise the nearLimiter (M42) nearLimiter headroom argument and the buffer-not-reservoir framing both depend on.

generatorMotorGap.rrMotorApplicability: e-4ORCE (AWD) only -- the FWD primary corpus carries the front motor and generator only, no rear motor.
generatorMotorGap.source: Article 2, Table 1 ("Specifications of the new e-POWER system", C-seg SUV column) and §3.1.
generatorMotorGap.note: Peak front-motor draw (150 kW) exceeds continuous generator output (116 kW) by 34 kW even before any rear-motor demand is considered. This is a manufacturer-specification-level, independent confirmation of the buffer thesis: the pack MUST supply the gap during any transient that pushes the motor toward its peak, which is exactly the mechanism the 55.5% blend-share finding (M41, S.blendShareMeanPct) and the Jun25 D4 worked example quantify from telemetry.

fixedPointOperation.source: Article 3, §3.1 ("Fixed-point operation, best fuel efficiency, and quietness"), Figs. 5-7.
fixedPointOperation.note: Manufacturer's stated steady-state operating point for this engine. Cross-check: this corpus's duration-weighted RPM occupancy chart (M82/M83, S.rpmDistribution) independently resolves a single dominant mode at 1900-2100 rpm covering ~62% of all engine-on time (split ~evenly 1900-2000 / 2000-2100) -- an unprompted field measurement landing almost exactly on the disclosed 2000 rpm design point, from a completely different method (raw 1 Hz telemetry vs. bench calibration).

engineFloor.statedFloorContext: exhaust system specifically designed around an operating range that does not use engine speeds below 1500 rpm
engineFloor.note: The corpus's own empirically-derived fuel-state classifier floor (M84, RPM_HIST_FUELSTATE_RPM_MIN) sits at 1400 rpm, measured directly from where boost/load cleanly separate fuelled from motored operation -- close to, and slightly below, the manufacturer's rounded 1500 rpm figure. The 300-1400 rpm band independently resolves as near-empty (~4% of engine-on time, a rev-through transient, M83), consistent with the stated floor; treat 1400 rpm as a field-measured refinement of the OEM's rounded number, not a contradiction of it.

maxOutputPoint.market: domestic (JDM) -- not confirmed identical for the EU-market FWD calibration this study's corpus is drawn from
maxOutputPoint.source: Article 3, §3.2 ("Maximum output point and quietness"), Fig. 8.
maxOutputPoint.note: VC-TURBO's variable compression ratio lets the max-output point sit at 4400 rpm instead of the ~5600 rpm a fixed-CR (10.5) engine would need to avoid knock at the same output -- 1200 rpm lower, ~3.5 dBA quieter under high load per the source. This study's own vmax-drive plateau (nearLimiter, M42) sits at ~4590 rpm, already past this stated max-output rpm, while calculated load (76.5% mean / 78.8% max) remained well below the corpus-pooled ceiling at that rpm band (92.2% max, S.nearLimiter.corpusCeiling) -- directionally consistent with a programmed speed limiter rather than an engine/generator output ceiling, though the JDM-figure caveat above means this is corroborating context, not an exact bound.

powerBlendingMechanism.source: Article 2, §5.2.2 ("Drive torque control matched to supercharged engine characteristics"), Fig. 10.
powerBlendingMechanism.note: Manufacturer's own description of the sequencing this study measures as "transient power blending": battery energy is drawn immediately on acceleration demand for fast response; the engine starts and, after the supercharging-response delay, its output is added on top of the battery's to continue building torque smoothly. This is the OEM-described mechanism behind the saw-tooth battery-power pattern in this study's Jun25 D4 worked example (repeated bursts to -49 kW under a hard ramp, engine running 95% of the time) and behind the ~55.5% mean blend-share finding (M41, S.blendShareMeanPct) -- a designed control behaviour, not an capability shortfall, exactly as this study's own sample-level decomposition concluded independently.

evRatioWltc.note: Manufacturer-cited engine-off time share on the WLTC cycle; a certification-cycle figure, not directly comparable to this corpus's mixed real-world engineOnHours/engineHoursByType figures, which are drawn from uncontrolled road driving across multiple drive classes rather than one standardized cycle. Provided as context, not as a target this study's own numbers are expected to match.

electricBrakeDissipationContext.note: The manufacturer describes exactly the mechanism this study's dissipationCensus/lowSpeedDissipation (M46/M48) measures -- after the pack reaches full charge, surplus regenerative energy that can no longer be absorbed was, in the prior-generation e-POWER system, dissipated by spinning the engine at high speed through the generator while braking. The new X-TRAIL adds an electric-controlled brake unit specifically to STOP regeneration once the pack is full and use friction braking instead, explicitly to suppress that engine speed increase and improve quietness. The motored unfuelled-dissipation signature this study still detects (knee ~77.5-80% SoC, ρ=0.68 SoC-vs-motored-seconds correlation) is therefore best read as the RESIDUAL path that still engages when regen exceeds pack acceptance despite the electric-brake mitigation -- not evidence that the mitigation is absent or ineffective, since this study has no visibility into how much additional dissipation the electric brake is diverting away from the engine before the motored signature is ever triggered.
